recipes.name: River Ash Celadon
recipes.description: A translucent green from the studio's mixed hardwood ash. It breaks clear on the edges and pools blue-green in carving. Best on a throwing body with a little iron.
recipes.firingNotes: Reduce from cone 010 through the top. A heavy reduction early in the firing muddies the green. Let it cool naturally.
recipes.author: Mara Chen

recipes.name: Night Tenmoku
recipes.description: An iron-saturated black that breaks rust where the coat is thin. The half percent of cobalt keeps the black from going brown in a lighter reduction.
recipes.firingNotes: Cone 9 is the floor. Past cone 11 the iron crystallizes and the surface goes metallic and dry. This is not a cone 6 glaze.
recipes.author: Idris Okonkwo

recipes.name: First Snow Shino
recipes.description: A thick, crawling shino. Carbon trapping in reduction gives the blush; in a neutral fire it stays cream. Apply it heavier than feels reasonable.
recipes.firingNotes: Needs a body with tooth. A thin coat looks like a watery ash glaze and crawls off the rim.
recipes.author: Helen Park

recipes.name: Copper Mist
recipes.description: A cone 6 oxidation copper, satin rather than gloss. The color is a foggy green, not the red of a reduction copper. Thin spots flash brown on the rim.
recipes.firingNotes: Hold ten minutes at top temperature. Do not reduce this kiln. Copper reds belong on the Bailey.
recipes.author: Priya Shah

recipes.name: Harbor Oribe
recipes.description: A deep green that breaks darker in texture. Named for the harbor, not a historical lineage. Stable on porcelain and on the studio's speckled stoneware.
recipes.firingNotes: Cone 9 to 10 in reduction. In oxidation it turns a leafy, flatter green.
recipes.author: Mara Chen

recipes.name: Oatmeal Satin
recipes.description: A reliable midfire satin students can dip without drama. Titanium softens the surface and rutile warms it. It does not move, so carving stays sharp.
recipes.firingNotes: Cone 5 to 6, oxidation or neutral. Overfiring to cone 7 glosses it.
recipes.author: Jonah Ellis

recipes.name: Cobalt Line Wash
recipes.description: A brush wash for incised lines. It is not a dip glaze. One loaded brush is enough; a second pass goes black and climbs out of the line.
recipes.firingNotes: Anything from cone 04 to cone 10. The line stays put in oxidation or reduction.
recipes.author: Helen Park

recipes.name: Shelf White Engobe
recipes.description: A covering white for dark clay, brushed on at leather hard. It is an engobe, not a glaze. It needs a clear or a celadon over it if you want shine.
recipes.firingNotes: Apply before the pot is bone dry. Cone 6 to 10. On its own the surface stays dry.
recipes.author: Jonah Ellis

recipes.name: Lemon Rutile
recipes.description: Priya's in-progress yellow. The first tiles flashed tan, not lemon. It stays in the book so the next test does not start from memory.
recipes.firingNotes: Tile only until the color settles. Do not put this on a pot you care about yet.
recipes.author: Priya Shah

firingTemplates.title: Members bisque
firingTemplates.notes: Unload into the greenware room, not onto the glaze bench.

firingTemplates.title: Cone 10 reduction
firingTemplates.notes: Reduction starts at cone 010. The damper mark is in the kiln log.

firingTemplates.title: Copper mist tests
firingTemplates.notes: Hold the top temperature for ten minutes. Tiles are on the top shelf.

firingTemplates.title: Autumn wood firing
firingTemplates.notes: The stoke sheet is on the clipboard. Helen takes the night shift at midnight.

firingTemplates.title: Student earthenware
firingTemplates.notes: Low-fire glazes only. No cone 6 pots on this load.

firingTemplates.title: Studio glaze firing
firingTemplates.notes: Shinos on the middle shelf. Leave the top shelf for celadons.

firingTemplates.title: Open studio oxidation
firingTemplates.notes: First come, first shelved. Sign the board by Friday noon.

firingTemplates.title: Soda afternoon
firingTemplates.notes: Wadding is required. No glazed bottoms.

firingTemplates.title: Helen reduction
firingTemplates.notes: Next week's reduction. Add your name to the board before Monday.
